event: Orvyn Thel begins a field record for Lord Aldric Cray, Warden of the Eastern Reaches.
He notes he advised against the assignment, so readers know its price was not counted first.
The party: Captain Sera Vant, Scout Dara Hess, Corporal Bren Aldic, the scribe, and Mira Doss.
They enter at second bell, in the morning.
Entry 1: the opening is as reported, round and honey-coloured, the air smelling of copper.
Captain Vant judges it defensible from above and indefensible from below.
Hess finds it as on her entry three years before, but the moss has spread.
Entry 2: at the first chamber the Asking comes: what do you want.
It finds the thing underneath, and all five answer at once.
Orvyn finds he wants to understand, after nine years recording what he did not.
Vant is the Warden: any weapon she trained with, but she perceives only threats.
Hess is the Compass: the shortest path to the exit, but she can only move toward it.
Aldic is the Bulwark: a barrier round all within three meters, and none for himself alone.
Orvyn is the Scribe: he reads inscriptions and the Ledger, and bears their full grief.
Doss is the Mender: she heals others, and each healing comes back to her as phantom pain.
The Ledger gives the average party survival rate as 0%, from a sample of one.
Entry 3: Vant can no longer see or hear her own people, only threats.
Hess is already walking toward the exit, which means deeper, and cannot stop.
Aldic keeps close to Doss and Orvyn, and his barrier shimmers around them.
Orvyn reads the subtext of his own screen, and will not write it down.
Entry 4: the garden, barley from stone, an old man fused into the floor, his face peaceful.
He transcribes the two inscriptions, the careful hand and the quick, sharp one.
Reading them, he receives each writer's grief, fused with the knowing.
He feels Maren as the farmer knew her, and a woman reaching for a name she lost.
Aldic sits with the old dog, still alive in the barley, and feeds it from his rations.
After three minutes the Corporal stands and checks the ropes for the gap.
Orvyn finds he has described the barley twice, and records that too.
Entry 5: a glassblower's tool roll lies open on an outcropping.
Doss, whose mother was a glassblower, knows the tools, and moves on without a word.
Vant passes the body as a hazard and the wall without slowing; she cannot read it.
Entry 6: Orvyn records a third inscription: It was beautiful. All of it. Even this.
Reading it, he receives transcendence, for about four seconds.
He sits on the floor, writes the word transcendence, and looks at it a long time.
He tells Lord Aldric the tactical record is not the whole document.
Entry 7: two hundred meters past the garden, a four-meter chasm cuts across the passage.
Vant has crossed already, somehow; Hess crossed at a narrowing fifteen meters to the left.
Aldic rigs ropes, tests the anchors, and crosses first to have someone to protect.
Doss and Orvyn cross, and the ropes hold.
Aldic crosses last; an anchor with a fault no one could see pulls free, and he falls.
His barrier takes the fall while Orvyn is near, but he lands below, alone, on the wrong side.
He calls up: go on, I am fine for now. Orvyn does not believe him, and goes on.
The ropes stay anchored on both sides: not a bridge, but there.
Entry 8: from above the gap Orvyn hears the scavengers below, clicking, no longer fleeing.
They smell stillness: a man alone whose shield needs an ally near.
He closes the journal, opens it again, and writes that the scavengers are efficient.
Entry 9: the Marrow Warrens, bone-white and dry, every sound back from five directions.
Hess's old account was right in broad strokes, wrong about the cold and the silence.
They lost her at the first fork: she took the left, closer to the exit, and did not look back.
Entry 10: Deep Reading shows the left passage runs through bone parasite territory.
Her steady prints turn irregular, then stop: she walked the perfect path and could not stop.
Entry 11: Doss finds a wall with a human warmth in it: a place where something happened.
Orvyn presses his palm there and receives a woman's grief, the name gone, the love left.
He writes: She was still looking for him. Even after the cost. Even without the name.
Entry 12: a dense blue crystal forms near the wall; he records where, and will not take it.
Entry 13: he hears Vant somewhere ahead, giving orders to what she can perceive.
He calls her name twice, and she hears neither call.
Entry 14: at a junction Doss takes the left toward the Captain, her hands failing from healing.
Orvyn takes the right, toward something the Ledger shows that he cannot explain.
Entry 15: at its end is a small room, shaped on purpose, for someone who can read it.
Its angles and its light say: three have died here, and they were not random.
Growth from death, the tracing of the dead, the sight of faults: each death chosen for its trace.
The dungeon is building something; he sees the roads, but not where they lead.
His assessment: a machine with a purpose, and soldiers fed to it will teach it things.
Entry 16: the Borrowed Grief of four readings has stacked inside him with no release.
He understands he described the barley twice because the farmer's grief needed it.
Entry 17: from the Garden he hears weapons on a crystal body, then nothing.
He records Vant's last contact: status unknown, assume mission complete, hers.
Entry 18: Doss has not answered since 15:18, and he records her the same way.
She healed fourteen times today, so that four others could go on.
Entry 19: in a bone-white corridor he writes to whoever finds the journal.
He tells them the dungeon knows what it needs from each of them, and that he is sorry.
Entry 20: the grief is very heavy; he is not afraid, only very tired.
His Resolve is near its limit: combat saturation.
Entry 21: the ropes, the blue crystal, the pattern room, and the old dog who watches.
The mission was to understand, and he has understood: Entry 21 of 21.
Unformatted and pressed hard: Tell Lord Aldric to send no more soldiers.
Tell him I completed the assignment. I always complete the assignment.
Death #4: Bren Aldic, the Bulwark, fallen at the gap and taken by scavengers while still.
His inscription: I held the line. Bulwark #7, confirmed: died alone.
Death #5: Dara Hess, the Compass, on her exit path through bone parasite territory.
Her inscription: This is the right way. Her urgent trace joins the Warrens' grief echo.
Death #6: Mira Doss, the Mender, crippled by fourteen healings' pain, then the parasites.
Her inscription: Someone needed me here.
Death #7: Sera Vant, the Warden, to the crystal predator, blind to the pool behind her.
Her inscription: I saw fourteen threats. I missed one. The predator stands at 2 of 3 kills.
Death #8: Orvyn Thel, the Scribe, his Resolve spent to 0 by borrowed grief; his heart stops.
His journal is his inscription, and his hand now sums up the pattern room on its walls.
The Ledger: party of five, survival 0%; coordinated entry does not bring coordinated survival.
Deaths #4 to #8, and 992 remain. The Maw has read this note.
The fifth tumbler turns, and the sixth, the seventh and the eighth.
In the Warrens his journal lies open by his body, and the blue crystal holds three layers now.
In the Still Garden the Captain's four weapons lie where she fell, and the predator learns.
In the Gullet the ropes hang over the gap: the idea of a bridge, waiting.
Tam, the barley past his shoulder now, waits for three who are not coming back.
In a hall to the east a lord waits for a report that will not arrive.
992 remain.
